newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea supplies 2 trln won to banks.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea supplies 2 trln won to banks.

text.p: The Bank of Korea said on Monday it supplied two trillion won to commercial banks by allowing them to cash in their Monetary Stabilisation Bonds ahead of maturity.
The move is to loosen the recent liquidity shortage faced by banks, an official at the central bank said.
The bonds were scheduled to mature on February 10, he said.
South Korea's three-month CD yields and overnight call rates have risen recently on fears of tighter liquidity after Hanbo Steel Co's debt default, dealers said.
Hanbo Steel failed to honour payments of more than five billion won last Thursday due to financial difficulties arising from excessive investment in facilities.
Dealers said the supply of funds was expected to ease overnight call rates to around 12.0 percent, compared with around 12.5 percent in morning trading on Monday.
